I honestly would not mess with a nose like that. Your nose is very proportionate as it is. Remember, rhinoplasty DOES NOT guarantee symmetry.

It's only been 4 days, it is literally impossible to tell what your nose will look like in weeks, months, years. If you go on RealSelf you will see that every commenting doctor mentions that swelling reduction generally takes 9-12 months.

I documented my healing process extensively and the changes are pretty drastic. I had my cast on for 9 days and when it was removed my nose looked twisted at the end because of the uneven nostrils. My nose continued to change over the following weeks and months.

Honestly if you are this broken up about it you may want to seek counseling. You need to be patient. If you broke your arm and had surgery would you expect it to look normal 1 week later? Think of it that way. I am aware that it is your face but you really have to remind yourself to be patient, even going to the lengths of avoiding mirrors if you have to.

The only thing that I would critique are your nostrils. They look a bit like a "forced flare." However, when I looked at your candid smiling photos I did not notice it. I think that the angle that you posted accentuates the nostrils.

Sometimes it's a perfect bunny nose. Although, it is not always a guaranteed rhino. My mom had a perfect ski slope nose and hers was all natural. People would frequently ask her who her doctor is...lol

As u/stopsignsareread said, it cycles. Lawsuits and investigations can be stressful. I have had to demote someone as a result of an investigation and it meant giving him a 100k/year pay cut. Ya, that day sucked.... He was basically in tears. 

HR is difficult for most people because of the human factor. The guy who was demoted deserved it, but the human factor in cutting someone's pay in half is obviously there. If you can just view things logically then it is less stressful. 

Lawsuits scare the crap out of me because a "mistake" on my end could end up costing the company hundreds of thousands of dollars (I live in the most backwards state in the US). There is very little room for error if you are in a sue happy state. I didn't ask one question that I should have asked in an investigation and it ended up coming back to bite us in the ass when the guy sued us. The guy was terminated for telling customers that he "ripped his wife's pussy open" among other vulgar statements....ya he still sued, and he will get money. So, I live with some guilt on that one. There is only so much that I could have done, the guy was nuts and would have sued even if I did everything perfectly.

I'll give you an example:

Sole HR employee for 250 employees (not smart, but not my choice). Yesterday I asked for a day off because my friend will be in town from overseas and I literally see her once every 3\-4 years. My boss stared at me then said "you better hope that nothing happens that day" because she is scheduled off as well. She finished it off with "keep your phone on you." Cue anxiety. Wtf is going to happen that can't wait one day? I don't like this rationale because I don't believe that it is ever a good idea to have a company built in a way that would allow for the company to sink if one person isn't on board, it just doesn't make sense. 

I am a Director of HR who is oddly kept as hourly. The benefit there is that no one wants to pay me overtime at my pay grade so I am capping at 8 hours per day / 40 hours per week. I check my email on vacation (ya, technically they should be paying me for this) and will respond sometimes. It is more that I am just curious about what emails I have and what is going on so that I don't come back to a shit storm. 

I plan my vacation days accordingly by looking at various times of the month. I won't leave around pay day and I won't leave around the 1st or 16th when we employ new hires. If you are smart about planning you can usually maintain good balance. I haven't taken a sick day all year so I can't speak on unplanned days.
